metadata.title: zERC20 Privacy Token Protocol - Formal Trust Model
metadata.description: Formal trust model defining actor trust levels and identifying trust boundary edges where data flows between actors of different trust levels.

actors.name: End User
actors.rationale: External users interacting via CLI or dApp are inherently untrusted. All user-provided inputs (amounts, addresses, proofs, requests) must be validated before processing.

actors.name: zERC20 Token Contract
actors.rationale: Core protocol smart contract under audit. Implements critical token logic with value constraints and hash chain integrity.

actors.name: Verifier Contract
actors.rationale: Core protocol smart contract under audit. Manages Nova/Groth16 proof validation and cross-chain coordination with cryptographic guarantees.

actors.name: Hub Contract
actors.rationale: Core protocol smart contract under audit. Central aggregation point with PoseidonT3 tree computation and LayerZero message handling.

actors.name: LiquidityManager Contract
actors.rationale: Core protocol smart contract under audit. Sole authority for minting/burning zERC20 with incentive curve enforcement.

actors.name: Adaptor Contract
actors.rationale: Core protocol smart contract under audit. Handles cross-chain exit coordination with slippage protection.

actors.name: Contract Owner/Protocol Admin
actors.rationale: Privileged EOA or multisig with immediate administrative powers. While authorized, key compromise enables complete protocol takeover. Must be treated as semi-trusted due to catastrophic compromise potential.

actors.name: Indexer Service
actors.rationale: Off-chain service providing Merkle proofs. Data it provides is used as witness inputs to ZK circuits but must be validated cryptographically on-chain.

actors.name: Decider/Prover Service
actors.rationale: Off-chain service converting Nova IVC to Groth16 proofs. Proofs are verified on-chain, but service availability and correct operation affect protocol liveness.

actors.name: LayerZero v2 Network
actors.rationale: External cross-chain messaging infrastructure. Relies on 13/19 guardian supermajority for message validation. Trusted for delivery but message content must be validated by receiving contracts.

actors.name: Stargate Bridge
actors.rationale: External cross-chain liquidity bridge. Protocol depends on Stargate security for asset bridging. Slippage limits provide some protection but bridge compromise affects funds.

actors.name: IC Key Manager Canister
actors.rationale: Internet Computer canister managing stealth address secrets. External infrastructure dependency for privacy-preserving operations.

actors.name: IC Storage Canister
actors.rationale: Internet Computer canister providing encrypted state storage. External infrastructure dependency; data is encrypted but availability depends on IC.

actors.name: Poseidon Hash Circuit
actors.rationale: Core cryptographic primitive using audited light-poseidon library with circom-compatible configurations. Mathematical soundness provides trust.

actors.name: Baby JubJub Curve Operations
actors.rationale: Core cryptographic primitive for zkSNARK-friendly elliptic curve operations. Mathematical soundness on BN254 embedded curve.

actors.name: Nova Folding Circuit
actors.rationale: Core cryptographic component using sonobe/folding-schemes library for incrementally verifiable computation. Mathematical soundness provides trust.

boundary_edges.description: Untrusted user submits wrap request with amount to trusted LiquidityManager contract.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The LiquidityManager must validate the wrap amount is within acceptable bounds, verify the user has sufficient underlying token balance, and ensure the value constraint (<=2^248-1) is satisfied before minting.

boundary_edges.description: Trusted LiquidityManager mints zERC20 tokens to untrusted user after wrap completion.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Token minting amount must be correctly calculated based on incentive curve. User receiving tokens is acceptable as they provided underlying collateral.

boundary_edges.description: Untrusted user submits unwrap request to trusted LiquidityManager contract.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The LiquidityManager must validate the unwrap amount, verify sufficient zERC20 balance, check liquidity availability, and correctly apply unwrap fees before burning tokens.

boundary_edges.description: Trusted LiquidityManager transfers underlying tokens to untrusted user after unwrap completion.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Underlying transfer amount must equal (original amount - fee). User receiving underlying is acceptable as they burned equivalent zERC20.

boundary_edges.description: Untrusted user initiates zERC20 transfer to trusted zERC20 contract.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The zERC20 contract must validate the transfer value satisfies the BN254 field constraint (<=2^248-1), verify sender has sufficient balance, and correctly update the hash chain.

boundary_edges.description: Semi-trusted Indexer receives IndexedTransfer events and builds Merkle tree.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Indexer receives authentic on-chain events. However, any Merkle proofs the Indexer generates must be verified cryptographically on-chain before being trusted.

boundary_edges.description: Untrusted user initiates stealth burn address generation locally.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Client-side stealth address generation. No trust boundary crossing as same untrusted actor.

boundary_edges.description: Untrusted user submits Nova IVC proof to semi-trusted Decider/Prover service.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: The Prover service must validate IVC proof format before processing. Malformed proofs should be rejected. Service should not trust user-provided metadata.

boundary_edges.description: Semi-trusted Prover service receives IVC proof from untrusted user.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Prover must deserialize and validate IVC proof structure. Invalid proofs must be rejected before consuming resources for Groth16 conversion.

boundary_edges.description: Untrusted user retrieves Groth16 proof from semi-trusted Prover service.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: User receives proof for on-chain submission. Proof will be verified on-chain by trusted Verifier contract, so semi-trusted source is acceptable.

boundary_edges.description: Untrusted user submits teleport request with Groth16 proof to trusted Verifier contract.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: CRITICAL BOUNDARY: The Verifier must fully validate the Groth16 proof, verify the transfer root reference exists, validate recipient hash binding, enforce monotonically increasing totalTeleported to prevent double-spend, and only then call teleport(). No trust in user-provided data until cryptographically verified.

boundary_edges.description: Trusted Verifier receives teleport request from untrusted user for processing.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All fields in the teleport request must be validated: proof data, root reference, recipient, and amount delta must pass cryptographic verification before any state changes.

boundary_edges.description: Untrusted user initiates cross-chain bridge via trusted Adaptor contract.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Adaptor must validate user has sufficient zERC20 balance before proceeding with unwrap and bridge operations.

boundary_edges.description: Trusted Adaptor receives unwrapAndBridge request from untrusted user.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Adaptor must validate all bridge parameters including destination chain, slippage limits, and refund address. Invalid parameters should cause revert.

boundary_edges.description: Trusted Adaptor sends underlying tokens via semi-trusted Stargate bridge.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Adaptor enforces slippage limits (minAmountOut) to protect against excessive bridge fees or manipulation. Stargate security is external dependency.

boundary_edges.description: Trusted Verifier sends proved transfer root to semi-trusted LayerZero network.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: LayerZero message contains authenticated transfer root. Receiving contracts must validate source endpoint ID (EID) to ensure message originated from authorized Verifier.

boundary_edges.description: Trusted Hub receives transfer root from semi-trusted LayerZero network.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: CRITICAL BOUNDARY: Hub must validate the source EID corresponds to a registered Verifier before accepting the transfer root. Unauthorized source EIDs must cause message rejection.

boundary_edges.description: Trusted Hub broadcasts aggregation root via semi-trusted LayerZero network.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Hub-computed aggregation root is sent to LayerZero. Receiving Verifiers must validate the source EID is the authorized Hub before storing global root.

boundary_edges.description: Trusted Verifier receives global root from semi-trusted LayerZero network.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: CRITICAL BOUNDARY: Verifier must validate the source EID is the authorized Hub contract before storing the global transfer root. Spoofed messages from unauthorized sources must be rejected.

boundary_edges.description: Trusted Verifier initiates cross-chain message via semi-trusted LayerZero.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Outbound messages to LayerZero are authenticated. LayerZero infrastructure handles delivery but message integrity depends on guardian supermajority.

boundary_edges.description: Semi-trusted LayerZero delivers validated message to trusted Hub.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Message has been validated by 13/19 guardian supermajority. Receiving contract must still validate source EID before processing payload.

boundary_edges.description: Semi-trusted LayerZero message requires EID validation by trusted Hub.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Hub validates incoming message source endpoint ID against registered Verifier list before accepting any payload data.

boundary_edges.description: Untrusted user retrieves historical Merkle proofs from semi-trusted Indexer.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: User receives Merkle proofs that will be used as witness data in ZK circuits. Proofs are verified cryptographically during circuit execution and on-chain verification.

boundary_edges.description: User submits Nova proof to trusted Verifier for transfer root proving.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: CRITICAL BOUNDARY: Verifier must validate the proof via IRootDecider.verifyOpaqueNovaProof(). The reserved hash chain checkpoint provides public input binding. Invalid proofs must be rejected.

boundary_edges.description: External caller (potentially untrusted) reserves hash chain checkpoint on trusted Verifier.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Checkpoint reservation binds the current zERC20 hash chain state. Verifier must read hash chain from trusted zERC20 contract, not from user input.

boundary_edges.description: Semi-trusted admin triggers verifier rotation on trusted Verifier contract during emergency.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Admin actions take effect immediately with no timelock. Key compromise enables malicious verifier rotation. This is an accepted risk with compensating controls (multisig, monitoring).

boundary_edges.description: Semi-trusted admin deactivates emergency state on trusted Verifier contract.
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Admin can re-enable normal operation after emergency. This requires trust that admin has resolved the underlying issue correctly.

critical_boundaries.description: All user interactions with protocol contracts (wrap, unwrap, transfer, teleport, bridge)
critical_boundaries.validation_requirement: All user inputs must be cryptographically validated or bounds-checked before state changes

critical_boundaries.description: LayerZero message passing between Hub and Verifier contracts
critical_boundaries.validation_requirement: Source endpoint ID (EID) must be validated against registered peer list before accepting any message payload

critical_boundaries.description: Interactions with Indexer and Prover services
critical_boundaries.validation_requirement: All data from off-chain services must be verified cryptographically on-chain (Merkle proofs, ZK proofs)
Admin key security is external to protocol. Multisig and monitoring are compensating controls
Slippage limits (minAmountOut) protect against excessive fees. Stargate security is external dependency
